clue.text: Copper drilling tool the length of one's forearm

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bit is the cutting tip fitted into a drill

explanation.surface: A copper drill bit described as being about as long as a forearm.
explanation.definitionFit: An old measure of length, taken from elbow to fingertip.

clue.text: Conservative shaped up — to accepted mores?

definitions.text: Conservative shaped up — to accepted mores?

parts.note: shaped means formed

explanation.surface: A Tory has been moulded into toeing the social line.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: a Conservative shaped to fit accepted ways.
explanation.definitionFit: To have complied with accepted rules or social standards.

clue.text: Where Wagner wrote two notes, then five, on operatic song

parts.note: B and A are two musical notes
V is the Roman numeral for five
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: An account of the composer writing music, note by note, for an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's festival theatre is at Bayreuth, in this German state.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern German state where the composer lived and built his opera house.

clue.text: Correct mark for a mattress cover

explanation.surface: Checking off a mattress cover as acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A check mark showing something is right; also the strong fabric case of a mattress or pillow.

clue.text: An unknown representation of the black knight

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure stands in for the sinister black knight.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess the knight is carved as a horse's head, so a black knight is pictured as a dark horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An unknown contender who may surprise everyone; also, literally, a horse of a dark colour, as the black chess knight is shaped.

clue.text: Crazy dance follows a bit of a fight

indicators.note: follows puts the dance after the bit of a fight

parts.note: a round is one stage of a boxing match
the twist is a 1960s dance

explanation.surface: A wild dance breaks out after a short scuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British phrase meaning mad or insane.

clue.text: Listen! Henry must have an animal house

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Noah's ark housed the animals

explanation.surface: Someone named Henry is told he needs a home for pets.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned command to pay attention to a sound.

clue.text: Horsemen surround a number of marauders

indicators.note: surround says the horsemen go around the other piece

parts.note: horsemen are riders

explanation.surface: Mounted men encircle a band of plunderers.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiders and marauders are both people who attack and plunder.

clue.text: Including me in the final part is correct

indicators.note: including says the final part holds the other piece inside

parts.note: the final part is the end

explanation.surface: Someone claims that putting themselves in the last section is right.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct and revise a text.

clue.text: Wholly virtuous probationers

explanation.surface: Trainees on trial are expected to be entirely pure.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO VICES, the word describes someone wholly virtuous.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with not a single moral failing; also beginners serving a trial period, as in a religious order.

clue.text: Good reasons for leaving the remainder of Turkish coffee

explanation.surface: Explaining why the dregs of a Turkish coffee are left in the cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid justifications; also the powerful sediment left at the bottom of a cup of thick coffee.

clue.text: Universal commendation may lift the spirits

parts.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal
commendation means praise

explanation.surface: Praise from everyone can cheer people up.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise up or elevate, here used of morale.

clue.text: Do they eat it in a Lesotho kraal?

definitions.text: Do they eat it in a Lesotho kraal?

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words Lesotho kraal, running across the gap

explanation.surface: A question about what is eaten in an African village enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: The vegetable is African in origin, so the question fits the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A green-podded vegetable, also called lady's fingers, native to Africa.

clue.text: Cold, discourteous and coarse

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
discourteous means rude

explanation.surface: A description of someone chilly, impolite and vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude and coarse are synonyms for vulgar or unrefined.

clue.text: Was obliged to be taken round Egyptian capital

indicators.note: taken round says one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: was obliged means had (to)
E is an abbreviation for Egyptian

explanation.surface: Someone had to be shown around Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egyptian capital' looks like Cairo, but Egyptian gives only E and capital alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital and head both mean the top part, as a column's capital is its head.

clue.text: A small, small house in Berkshire

definitions.note: a phrase naming a place in that county, standing for the town

parts.note: a cot is a small cottage

explanation.surface: A tiny little cottage in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a town in Berkshire, a county west of London, famed for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berkshire town known for its royal horse racing.

clue.text: Even in retrospect it looks the same

indicators.text: in retrospect it looks the same
indicators.note: says the word reads the same backwards as forwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something smooth looks no different when you look back on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and level both mean flat or equal.

clue.text: Dining car fare for the disabled

definitions.text: Dining car fare for the disabled

parts.words: Dining car fare for the disabled
parts.note: reads like food served in a railway buffet car, but means meals delivered by vehicle to housebound people

explanation.surface: Food served in a train's restaurant carriage for disabled passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is a service bringing hot meals by van to the elderly and housebound.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery scheme taking cooked food by road to people who cannot shop or cook.

clue.text: Retreat from a Saint Petersburg museum

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws from a famous Russian gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A secluded dwelling of a recluse; also the great art museum in the former Winter Palace.

clue.text: Telepath has nevertheless to walk with hesitation

parts.note: nevertheless means though
to walk means to tread
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A mind-reader who nonetheless walks haltingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who claims to perceive others' minds without speech.

clue.text: Ballistic missile carried by Britannia

explanation.surface: Britannia is depicted holding a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The submarine-launched missile in Britain's nuclear deterrent; also the three-pronged spear held by Britannia on old coins.

clue.text: Drive back after a dance, despite lack of agreement

indicators.note: after puts the reversed piece following the dance

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for drive is turned round

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in addresses

explanation.surface: People drive home after a night out despite quarrelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife or disharmony between people.

clue.text: Keen for opera star to make a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means the word for opera star is read backwards

parts.note: a diva is a leading female opera singer

explanation.surface: Fans are eager for a singer to return to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and avid both mean eager or enthusiastic.

clue.text: A sober man in charge of ancient Athens

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a teetotaller

explanation.surface: A clean-living man takes command of the ancient Greek city.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to Attica, the region of the classical Greek city-state.

clue.text: A policeman with sex appeal needs to be punished

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An attractive police officer is due for a reprimand.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal comes from 1920s slang, the 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom meaning get into trouble or be punished.

clue.text: Like knocking back Italian wine

parts.note: like means as

indicators.note: knocking back says the abbreviation for Italian is turned round

explanation.surface: Someone is drinking Italian wine as if it were water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' suggests drinking, but it turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkling wine from Piedmont in northern Italy.

clue.text: Roman bones found in a Greek mountain

explanation.surface: Ancient Roman skeletons are discovered on a Greek peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin plural for bones; also a mountain in Thessaly from Greek myth.

clue.text: Eastern border uprising establishes Arab leader

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising means the word for border is read upwards

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A revolt on the eastern frontier installs a new Arab ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim ruler or commander, as in the Gulf states.

clue.text: One tsar confounded by gross betrayal

indicators.note: confounded means mixed up, so the letters of One tsar are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Russian ruler is overthrown by an act of treachery.
explanation.definitionFit: The gravest form of disloyalty, betraying one's country or ruler.

clue.text: Fair game in which Thomas returns a high ball

parts.note: Tom is short for Thomas

indicators.note: returns means the words a high ball are read backwards

parts.note: a lob is a ball hit high in the air

explanation.surface: Thomas returns a lofted shot during a game at the fete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reads like a tennis stroke but turns A LOB into BOLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle-style game of chance common at British fetes and fairs.

clue.text: Albigensians go to Isaiah for purification

parts.note: the Albigensians were a medieval heretical sect also called Cathars
Is is the abbreviation for the Book of Isaiah

explanation.surface: Medieval heretics consult the prophet in search of cleansing.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotional or spiritual cleansing, from the Greek for purging.

clue.text: A long pile of earth in Bridgetown

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the word Bridgetown

explanation.surface: Someone notices a heap of soil in the Barbados capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A long raised strip of soil or land, like a ploughed furrow's crest.
